title: T1071.003 — Application Layer Protocol - Mail Protocols
subtitle: The animation shows the example intrusion in eight steps.
aria: T1071.003 - Application Layer Protocol - Mail Protocols

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Loader lands
steps.caption: A phished loader - a small program that installs malware - runs on the laptop FIN-WS-04 at 10.20.4.17. It is written in Visual Basic Script (VBS). It skips the corporate relay and signs in to the attacker mail server mail.attacker-mail[.]com (198.51.100.60) on port 587 with hard-coded credentials. Zeek shows a workstation speaking SMTP directly to the internet. That single connection is the clearest start signal
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

fields.detail: A phished loader - a small program that installs malware - runs on the laptop FIN-WS-04 at 10.20.4.1

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Mail-shaped C2
steps.caption: The malware sends task results as mail bodies and picks up its next orders from replies that carry attachments. A .jpg attachment is really a RAR archive with a new module. the client user-agent reads Pterodo/1.0, not Outlook - a free, high-value tell that survives STARTTLS encryption
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Data out as attachments
steps.caption: The malware splits stolen documents into 14 mails of 4 to 8 MB each and sends them to the same attacker mailbox as fake .jpg attachments. 78 MB leaves one host in minutes. Volume plus receiver domain makes exfiltration easy to score
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Tasking via IMAP
steps.caption: The operator writes commands into a Drafts folder. Every five minutes the malware logs in over IMAP 993, reads the drafts, and sends nothing back from that folder. a workstation polling IMAP on a fixed schedule is rare enough to alert on by itself
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Relay abuse attempt
steps.caption: The malware also tries the corporate relay smtp.fin-example.com, spoofing the sender finance@fin-example.com. The relay demands authentication and rejects the attempt nine times. relay auth failures that come from a client IP point to stolen or guessed mail credentials
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Alert fires
steps.caption: The egress rule "workstation to external SMTP or IMAP" fires. The SIEM (the platform that stores logs and fires alerts) joins the two views: network and mail gateway. The host receives legitimate mail but sent 78 MB with no legitimate cause. one alert plus one join turns a suspicious flow into a likely incident
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Confirm and scope
steps.caption: The analyst pulls Zeek smtp.log for the host: one receiver domain, one consistent user-agent, subjects that look like finance reports. Neighbor hosts show no similar sessions. hunting the user-agent and the domain across 30 days gives a clean scope: one host
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Contain
steps.caption: The SOC blocks attacker-mail[.]com at the egress firewall and the mail gateway, isolates FIN-WS-04, rotates the mailbox credentials, and turns on deny-all outbound SMTP from user ranges. the policy fix matters most. The next loader will find a closed door
